validated_work_order.approach:
Two files. One declaration in the stylesheet, and one abstraction in the test file that every stylesheet pin in it then uses, so that at the end of this change there is no second CSS parser left in the suite. Plus the repair that makes the suite green so any of it can be verified. The diagnosis is settled and this round does not reopen it. What this round changes is R5 (new: the collection policy for the `#main:focus` pair, which the plan mandates migrating and never states), the bounds on two stated arguments, and one criterion's numbers.

R1 — ONE RULE ABOUT THE TERMINATING SEMICOLON, STATED ONCE. `declarations(body, prop)` treats a trailing chunk after the last `;` as a declaration, and every pin that reads through it therefore stays GREEN when a declaration loses its terminator. It is a STATED LOOSENING, stated in one place (AC-5) and quoted nowhere else except where a mutation is derived from it. Matrix mutation 9 (the `;` off `.page-title`'s `line-height: 1.25`) is GREEN and mutation 10 (the `;` off `#main > *`'s `min-width: 0`) is GREEN. What guards `#main > *`'s terminator afterwards is nothing, and out_of_scope says so in those words with the CSS rule that makes it correct — a declaration's terminating `;` is optional when it is the last one in a block, so `.page-title { margin: 0; line-height: 1.25 }` and the same rule with the semicolon are identical to every browser. A pin that reddens on the difference is a pin on punctuation rather than on the property it exists to protect, which is the defect class this ticket was filed about.

R2 — `.page-title` READS THROUGH `declarations()` TOO, so there is one reader rather than two behaviours. Today it is `const rule = /\.page-title\s*\{([^}]*)\}/.exec(css)` plus three `assert.match(rule[1], /prop:\s*value\s*;/)` calls — first-match only, terminator-required. After this change it collects EVERY non-nested rule whose comma-split selector part is exactly `.page-title` and asserts `declarations(rule.body, 'margin')` deepEqual `['0']`, `'font-size'` deepEqual `['1.4rem']`, `'line-height'` deepEqual `['1.25']` on each. This is what makes mutation 9 GREEN under R1, and it is a strict improvement: appending `.page-title { margin: 4rem; }` is green under first-match and breaks the page. The conversion preserves the assertion's meaning, so it is not an exception to AC-6, which constrains meaning and not spelling; AC-6 names it anyway.

R3 — THE SIX EXISTING PINS KEEP NESTED RULES IN THEIR MIGRATED COLLECTIONS. This is the correction that costs the most if an implementer gets it wrong. Today all six collect their rules with `[...css.matchAll(/<selector>\s*\{([^}]*)\}/g)]`, which matches a rule wherever it sits, including inside an `@media` block. The coverage is live rather than theoretical: appending `@media (max-width: 900px) { .table-scroll { overflow-x: visible; } }` to src/web/styles.css reads 70 pass / 2 fail, the extra failure being test 66. The new pin collects NON-NESTED rules, because the media-nested `.awaiting-list li` rule must not be dragged into a value assertion. An implementer who applies that filter to the six as well — the natural reading of 'one reader, one rule' — silently deletes six live nested-override checks and the suite goes green on exactly the defect this ticket exists to close. So: the six keep EVERY rule, top-level or nested, that matches their selector; the non-nested filter belongs to the new `.awaiting-list` pin alone. Matrix mutation 12 pins it and is the one row a single implementer command settles.

R4 — THE REPAIR FOR THE PRE-EXISTING RED USES THE FILE'S OWN IDIOM. Replace `/<li class="approval-card">/` with the token test the card pin already uses fifteen lines below it: extract the class attribute, split it on whitespace, assert the resulting Set contains `approval-card`, and separately assert the element carries `data-testid="approval-card"` per .sdlc/memory/qa/selectors.md. The regex `/<li\b[^>]*\bclass="[^"]*\bapproval-card\b[^"]*"/` is NOT used: it accepts `<li class="approval-card-extra">` and `<li class="not-approval-card">` where the form it replaces rejects both, because `\b` after `approval-card` matches at a hyphen boundary. That is a new false negative on the rename axis #71 finding 2 was filed about, in the file that documents the lesson, and the token form is immune to it while still matching the shipped markup.

R5 — THE `#main:focus` PAIR GETS A STATED COLLECTION POLICY EACH. This is the gap this round closes and v11 left to the implementer, with the two candidate readings failing in opposite directions.

  The 345 pin collects every rule whose comma-split selector part is exactly `#main:focus` AND that is NOT nested, requires the collection NON-EMPTY, and asserts `declarations(body, 'outline')` deepEqual `['none']` on each. TOP LEVEL ONLY, and the reason is the file, not taste: styles.css has two such rules — 131 at top level with `outline: none` and 136 nested inside the `@media (forced-colors: active)` opened at 135 with `outline: 2px solid CanvasText` — and the other test in the pair owns the second one at a different value. Collecting both and asserting `none` on each false-reds the shipped file, which is the one thing a migration must not do.

  The 359 pin collects every NESTED rule whose selector part is exactly `#main:focus`, requires it non-empty, asserts `declarations(body, 'outline')` deepEqual `['2px solid CanvasText']` on EACH, and compares the two rules' SOURCE INDICES rather than the character offsets the file uses today. This is strictly stronger than the assertion it replaces (which checks the first carve-out only) and it is what closes the first-match blind spot: the pin today is `const rule = /#main:focus\s*\{([^}]*)\}/.exec(css)` with no `g`, so `@media (max-width: 900px) { #main:focus { outline: auto; } }` appended to the stylesheet is invisible to it and the suite stays green. Under R5 that mutation is red, because the rule is nested and does not carry the carve-out value. It also keeps the `length > 0` guard on the not-at-top-level lookup, so a reader regression that stopped descending into at-rules cannot make the test pass vacuously on a file with no carve-out at all, and it re-sources the `bareRuleAt !== -1` guard from the reader rather than leaving it on raw text, where it silently changes meaning once the comment strip is in play (styles.css:117 mentions `#main:focus` in prose).

  One consequence to state because it moved: the forced-colors pin's OLD regex `/@media\s*\(forced-colors:\s*active\)\s*\{[^@]*?#main:focus\s*\{([^}]*)\}/` only found the carve-out when it was the first thing in the block, so the reader's rewrite is strictly MORE PERMISSIVE and matrix mutation 18 is GREEN on purpose. 'Another nested rule before the carve-out' now means a rule with a DIFFERENT selector — a second `#main:focus` rule in the block is RED under the per-rule value assertion, which is the correct verdict and is stated so the row cannot be read two ways.

A. Add `overflow-wrap: anywhere;` to the EXISTING `.awaiting-list li` rule in src/web/styles.css, in place among its display / gap / border / border-radius / padding declarations. Do NOT add a second rule with the same selector that RE-DECLARES the property: the new pin collects every non-nested rule on that selector whose body declares the property and asserts the value on each, so such a rule joins the collection and reads RED against the VALUE assertion (matrix mutation 3a) — that is the mechanism, and it is NOT `conflictingOverrides`, which exempts the whole collected set by design and can never report a rule that joined it. A second rule on the same selector that leaves `overflow-wrap` alone is not collected and is GREEN (mutation 3b), which is correct: a rule that neither declares `overflow-wrap` nor uses the `all` shorthand cannot change that property's computed value. The `all` bound is not decoration — `.awaiting-list li { all: revert; }` declares no overflow-wrap, so the collection and the conflict helper both skip it, and `all` resets the property to its initial value and reinstates the overflow with a green suite. The stylesheet already uses a `*` rule (styles.css:25), so the shorthand is in house style. The bound is recorded in out_of_scope rather than pinned; nobody is writing `all: revert` on a list item, but the claim as previously written was universal and is not.

B. Add four shared helpers near the top of test/web/pages.test.js, beside H1_HOOK (line 23) and mainOf (line 37), and route all eight stylesheet read sites through them. Only the plumbing moves, with the changes named in AC-6 named explicitly.

  `readStylesheet()` — the single readFileSync of src/web/styles.css, returning the SOURCE STRING. Every one of the eight sites becomes `const css = readStylesheet();`, the shape they have today, and the parse is one call on top. It returns the string rather than the parsed rules on purpose: the `length > 0` guards and failure messages at lines 1656, 1664, 1702, 1760, 1767, 1804 and 1821 are about the file, and AC-4's greps then mean exactly what they say. Line 1611's readFileSync is NOT migrated: it reads test/web/pages.test.js itself inside the H1_HOOK call-site pin.

  `cssRules(source)` — strip /* */ with the SAME expression the card pin uses today at line 1696 (`css.replace(/\/\*[\s\S]*?\*\//g, ' ')`), then walk with a brace stack. A frame whose selector starts with '@' is a BLOCK whose children are rules; any other frame is a rule whose body is declarations. ';' terminates a declaration inside a rule and a prelude inside an at-rule. Nested rules are emitted with their own selector and a `nested` flag meaning 'not at top level'. At-rule frames are not emitted. Every rule carries a source index. ONE EXCEPTION, and it is in the shipped file today: a block whose prelude is `@keyframes` (or `@-webkit-keyframes`) contains KEYFRAME STEPS, not style rules — skip its children entirely rather than emitting `0%` / `100%` as rules, which the generic branch would otherwise do. A `0%` selector matches nothing on a comma-split `===` comparison, so the mis-emission is harmless to every pin today, but it puts junk into the one structure every other helper depends on and the shipped file has a keyframes block at styles.css:336-340, so the spec is wrong as written and cheap to make right. TWO OTHER FAILURE MODES PRODUCE PLAUSIBLE OUTPUT AND NEITHER SHOWS UP UNTIL A PIN DEPENDS ON IT: accumulating the prelude through a rule body concatenates `width: 100vw;` onto the selector of the next nested rule, and a reader that appends nested text to the parent body instead of descending into it drops every nested rule and reinstates the at-rule blind spot exactly — matrix mutations 4 and 11 are both green under that second bug while passing every test in the file as written today. This order pins NO magic rule count: a total breaks on every future stylesheet edit for no semantic reason and would not have caught either.

  `declarations(body, prop)` — one property's values from an already comment-stripped body, anchored on a declaration boundary (start of body, or after a ';') rather than a bare substring, with a trailing chunk after the last ';' treated as a declaration. THE REASONS FOR THE ANCHORING ARE MEASURED, and one commonly cited reason is false: 'min-width' is NOT a substring of 'min-height'. The reasons that are real, both green today: (a) a rule with no min-width at all but a comment naming one reads as ['16ch'], count 1, GREEN — the BUG-1 state passing the BUG-1 pin, because the min-width pin does not strip comments while the card pin beside it does; (b) a comment standing beside a real declaration is consumed as the declaration, so widths comes back ['0','16ch'] where the real floor is 16ch. The third thing the boundary buys is the custom-property case: a bare substring search matches `--min-width: 16ch` and a boundary-anchored one does not, in a stylesheet whose `:root` declares seventeen custom properties. The trailing-chunk clause is R1 and nothing else.

  `conflictingOverrides(rules, pinned, selectors, prop)` — the card pin's override loop at lines 1717-1720, lifted out of that test's body and corrected. The property is a fourth argument and the filter `declarations(other.body, prop).length > 0` runs INSIDE, because the card pin's existing `/overflow-wrap\s*:/` filter at line 1699 is what makes the comment above it true — a rule that cannot override the card classes does not turn the suite red. Take the property away and you get one of two failures: drop the filter and a narrow-viewport padding tweak on a pinned selector turns the suite red for a declaration that cannot change the property, re-breaking a tolerance #71 added on purpose; or hardcode overflow-wrap inside and the non-wrap pins get a check that can never fire. `pinned` is the rule or the SET of rules the calling pin has already asserted on, and every member is exempt — without the exemption the fix itself would be reported as an override of itself. A conflict is reported for any rule other than the pinned set, at ANY source index, top-level or nested, declaring `prop` on a comma-split selector part equal to a member of `selectors`. Symmetric in source order, because an override authored above the pinned rule wins at narrow viewports exactly as one below does. The nested half is the fix for review finding 3 and is matrix mutations 4 and 14.

  THE SELECTOR LOOKUP MUST ANCHOR ON THE SELECTOR'S END — compare a comma-split part to the pinned selector with `===`, never `selector.includes(pinnedSelector)`. '.opportunity-roww' and '.tenant-names' both contain their pinned selector as a substring; the current `\s*\{` anchors give the pins their rename protection today, and a substring lookup deletes it across all eight pins at once, invisibly. Matrix mutation 16 is the GREEN that proves it survives.

  WHERE THE CONFLICT CHECK IS CALLED, and this is the design decision that matters most. Call it at the card pin (1691) and at the new `.awaiting-list` pin ONLY. Lines 1652 (`#main > *`), 1663 (`.table-scroll`), 1756 (`.approval-actions`), 1766 (`.approval-actions input`), 1801 (`.journal-drawer-body`) and 1818 (`.tenant-name`) each already collect EVERY rule matching their selector — top-level and nested, per R3 — and assert the property on every one of them, so their every-match loop IS their selector's override check, and it is stronger than a same-selector conflict check because it also catches a rule declaring the WRONG value. Because the helper exempts the pinned set, and on those six the pinned set is every rule that could ever match, a call there could never fire: dead code that reads as coverage. Put one comment line in each of those six tests saying the every-match loop is that selector's override check, so the absence reads as a decision. The distinction is pinned by contract case 10 so it cannot rot silently.

  THE CARD PIN KEEPS ITS OWN PRE-FILTER — the one place a migration could false-red on a correct stylesheet. Today the card pin builds its candidate set, filters it with `/overflow-wrap\s*:/.test(rule.body)`, and only then calls `.find()`. That filter is load-bearing: without it `find()` returns `.approval-card, .experiment-card` at styles.css:375-383 — the border / padding / display rule, two classes, no `overflow-wrap` at all — and both the selector-set equality assertion against CARD_CLASSES and the `deepEqual(values, ['anywhere'])` assertion go RED on the shipped file. This pre-filter is DISTINCT from the one inside `conflictingOverrides`, and both survive the migration. It is named in AC-6 so nobody simplifies it away.

  THE NEW `.awaiting-list` PIN, in the house style of `#main > *` and `.tenant-name` rather than a whole-body assertion, and in ONE test. In order: (a) collect every rule that is NOT nested, whose comma-split selector part is `.awaiting-list` or `.awaiting-list li`, and whose body DECLARES overflow-wrap — the property filter is part of the COLLECTION predicate, not only inside the helper, and the test's comment must say that in those terms, because the media-nested rule's selector part IS exactly '.awaiting-list li' and an unfiltered collection takes it in, at which point `deepEqual(['anywhere'])` fails and the suite goes red for a padding declaration; (b) require the collection NON-EMPTY, with a message that says so, so deleting the declaration and leaving a comment is red (mutation 1), and today's `.awaiting-list li` rule has zero overflow-wrap declarations in it, so (b) is what turns the current state red rather than vacuous; (c) require each collected rule's overflow-wrap values to deepEqual `['anywhere']`; (d) run `conflictingOverrides(rules, collected, ['.awaiting-list', '.awaiting-list li', '.awaiting-list li strong', '.awaiting-list li span'], 'overflow-wrap')` and require it to report nothing. TWO STRICTNESSES WITH THEIR COSTS RECORDED. First, the selector list in (d) is a SNAPSHOT of the awaiting li's element children in src/web/pages.js:695-699 — `<strong>` and `<span>`, and I read that markup — not an exhaustive set: a third element child carrying free text is invisible to the conflict check with a green suite, which is the descendant hole (mutations 7 and 8) in the selector list rather than in the descendant. Deriving the list from the rendered markup in the test's own render half would close it, and is named as a follow-up rather than built here, because the derive-it check is new machinery for a case nobody has hit and the hole it closes is already named, demonstrated by QA on purpose, and in residual_risks. Second, the collection requires the declaration at TOP LEVEL, because a fix authored only inside `@media (max-width: 900px)` satisfies the new pin in full AND satisfies the whole browser sweep at 320 / 375 / 414, all of which are inside that query, while the defect is not inherently narrow-viewport (mutation 5, RED on purpose). Separately, the parent `.awaiting-list` is in the collection's selector set because `overflow-wrap` is inherited and the pin must not report a correct fix on the parent as absent (mutation 6, GREEN on purpose).

  (e) the render half, in the same test, AS A LINK ASSERTION AND NOTHING MORE. Use `seededRepos(prefix)`, which creates tenant_demo and the seeded decisions, NOT bare `freshRepos()`, which has no tenant: on a seeded fixture `repos.tenants.list()` reads exactly `['tenant_demo']`, and `decisionsOf` at src/web/pages.js:614-619 is `if (!tenant) { return []; }`, so a fixture without a tenant renders the empty branch with no `class="awaiting-list"` anywhere. Before rendering, assert that `repos.tenants.list()` is exactly one row and its id is `tenant_demo`, with a message saying the fixture's tenant selection is load-bearing for `firstTenant()` — that assertion stops a future seed adding a second tenant from repointing the whole page, and it is the same check that proves a seeded database was served. Then create ONE further decision on top of the seed through the EIGHT-FIELD `repos.decisions.create(...)`, whose decision_id is `'dec_' + 'q'.repeat(136)` (140 unbreakable characters), and assert that /journal at override 'partial' emits `class="awaiting-list"` with at least one `<li data-decision-id` and that the long id appears inside the awaiting `<ul>` segment. Count assertions are NON-EQUALITY throughout: on this fixture the page carries `data-decision-id` ten times, and the id also reaches the journal table row and the Open button, so the page's count is hostage to an unrelated seed edit. The claim is 'the list renders and the id is in it', not a count.

  (f) the twenty-row mutation list ALSO LIVES IN THE FILE, as a comment block above the new pin. A matrix that exists only in a plan document is deleted with the plan and enforces nothing; the one durable home available to this change is the test it pins. C2 comma-split selectors: `a, b { color: red; }` yields selector parts ['a','b'] and a lookup on 'b' finds the rule. WHAT I UPHELD, AND THE FIRST IS THE FOURTH OF ITS CLASS.
